verdict: The library holds up under its own tests: 177 pass and 2 are skipped as needs-app. 13 of 14 mutations are caught. Every mechanism the brief names fails a test when it is broken: stale-break verification, alive-null counted as alive, chain link (written and verified), fence/updateRow CAS, writeTasks rev CAS, staging-cut prefix hash, READY exclusion, nlink link detection, atomic rename, rename retry, additionalProperties, required, temp nonce. One mutation survives: appendLedger's re-check of the lock just before the write (lib.mjs:1485). Two defects can break a LIVE lock. First, realProc.alive answers false (dead) when the CIM query fails; this was reproduced: the query printed NONE and PowerShell exited 0. Second, the own-clock start time is compared symmetrically within a 2 s tolerance. A broken live lock means two writers, so the ledger chain can fork and the task table can lose an update. Also medium: one PowerShell per lock contention; an empty or unparseable lock blocks forever; the T21 test leaks its reader child when the writer fails (it hung a mutation run until the lane's 300 s timeout); card.quote's 15-word cap has no length bound. No high or medium defect was found in the hash chain itself, the fence CAS, the staging cut, temp naming, the validator's keyword handling or the transcript parser's counting against probes/transcript-format.md. psOne interpolates only an integer pid. No wall-clock read stands where a counter is meant. Full return: C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/192654871f6b1294/e24f17dc-4aea-4914-a9d1-280a723d620e/scratchpad/tcb-build/done/lib-review.json

findings.claim: realProc.alive returns false (dead) when Get-CimInstance fails, so a waiter breaks a live holder's run.lock or watcher.lock. Contract 4.4/4.9 says a PowerShell failure is null, which counts as alive. list() likewise returns [] instead of throwing proc-unavailable.
findings.evidence: psOne runs `$x=Get-CimInstance ...; if($x){...} else {'NONE'}`. A failed CIM query is non-terminating, so $x is $null, 'NONE' is printed and powershell exits 0. Reproduced with the same script shape and a failing query: stdout NONE, exit 0, the CimException only on stderr. alive() then returns false (line 2689) and isStale returns true. breakStale's re-read matches the record judged stale, so the waiter takes the lock and appends lock-break. A holder already between assertHeld and its append, or inside release() (read nonce, then unlink), then writes against the new holder: two seq n+1 lines, or a lost tasks.json update. In PS_LIST the same failure leaves $p=@(), so list() returns [] with exit 0: stop verify sees no survivors and slotCount sees no live process.
findings.fix: Prefix PS_LIST, PS_BOOT and psOne with `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop';` (or add -ErrorAction Stop to each Get-CimInstance). A failed query then exits 1, execFileSync throws, and alive returns null, list throws proc-unavailable 2, boot returns null. Add a test through a realProc seam.

findings.claim: The lock record's own-clock start time (Date.now() minus process.uptime()) is matched to the CIM CreationDate symmetrically within 2 s. A live holder whose start-up took more than 2 s, or whose wall clock stepped after its creation, is judged dead and its lock is broken.
findings.evidence: process.uptime() counts from Node's own start, after the exe is loaded; CreationDate is when Windows created the process. The lane runs everything at below-normal priority, and the PC stalls under memory pressure and a scanner, so a start-up delay over 2 s is plausible. sameStartTime then returns false, alive returns false, and the lock is broken, with the same fork consequence as LR-1. T85 checks the gap only on an idle machine.
findings.fix: Compare one-sided for lock holders: same process iff listed CreationDate <= recorded start + START_TOLERANCE_MS. A pid reused by a later process is still told apart, because it was created after the holder recorded its start; a slow start-up no longer reads as dead.

findings.claim: Every waiter that finds a lock held by a holder it has not judged yet spawns one powershell.exe (about 2 s). The record it judges was read before that call, and the rename comes after it.
findings.evidence: isStale runs on every 'exists' iteration; the cache only dedupes by nonce. Ordinary contention (watcher plus status, replace or commit) therefore launches PowerShell once per distinct holder seen: the short-lived process bursts that preceded the PC stalls. With a truly stale lock and several waiters, the 2 s-old judgement often renames a fresh holder's lock. The restore path then runs; during it that holder gets lock-lost and a third process can slip in, turning the restore into an .orphan.
findings.fix: Judge a holder only after the same nonce has been seen unchanged for K consecutive retries (a counter, for example 50, about 5 s). Re-read the lock bytes right before the rename in breakStale and skip the break if they changed.

findings.claim: An empty or unparseable lock file is never judged stale, so every script exits 75 until a person deletes it.
findings.evidence: tryCreate opens with wx, then writes and fsyncs. A hard reset in between (frequent on this PC) can leave a zero-length run.lock. readLockRecord then returns record null, isStale(null) is false, and acquireLock throws lock-busy 75 on every later call by every script. Neither status (which reports only .orphan) nor handover (which cleans *.stale and *.orphan) names it.
findings.fix: When the raw lock bytes stay unparseable and unchanged across the whole retry budget (a counter), break the lock with the same rename / compare-bytes / create protocol and append lock-break {stale: null, bytes}. At the least, report a 'lock-unreadable' anomaly in status.

findings.claim: Removing appendLedger's re-check of the lock right before the write (lib.mjs:1485, handle.assertHeld()) fails no test, although it is the guard against forking the chain after the lock was lost during the tail read (contract 4.4: assertHeld before every write).
findings.evidence: Mutation M11 (line 1485 replaced by `void 0;`): T39-T47 through the lane gave 9 pass, 0 fail. Only the entry assertHandle (1443) is exercised by T42.
findings.fix: Add a test that uses setFsSeam({openSync}) to overwrite run.lock with another nonce when tailInfo opens the ledger, and expects lock-lost 75 with the ledger bytes unchanged. Do the same for writeTasks between its rev read and writeAtomic (1609).

findings.claim: T21 never ends its reader child when writeAtomic throws: the test hangs and leaves a live node process.
findings.evidence: The child is spawned at 792. The stop file and await come only after the 200 writes (799-801), with no try/finally. Under mutation M5b, writeAtomic threw, the reader kept running, and the run hung until the lane's 300 s timeout (exit 124, review-tmp/lib/out-M5b.txt).
findings.fix: Wrap the writes in try { ... } finally { fs.writeFileSync(stop,'1'); if (child.exitCode === null) child.kill(); await closed; } and assert after the finally.

findings.kind: validator accepts what the format forbids
findings.claim: card.quote ('<=15w', CONTRACT 3.1) has x-maxWords 15 but no maxLength. wordCount splits only on JS \s, so a quote with no \s separators (CJK text, words joined by U+200B or U+2060) of any length passes as one word.
findings.evidence: /\s+/u does not match U+200B or U+2060: 'a​b​...' with 500 tokens gives wordCount 1, and a CJK paragraph counts as 1 to 15 words. No maxLength exists on quote, so the 15-word cap, which keeps quotes short and pack tokens bounded, fails silently.
findings.fix: Add a maxLength to quote (for example 200 code points) and to the other x-maxWords fields, or make wordCount also split on \p{Cf} and count CJK characters as words.
